opener_concept: Two shopping trolleys (10 kg empty, 50 kg full) given the SAME shove: the light one speeds up more. The student computes a = F/m for each (100/10 = 10, 100/50 = 2), which IS F = ma rearranged, before the equation is named.

problems_fixed.what: Duplicate solution within tier: silver[1] (change in momentum) and silver[3] (force) both stored 18000. Changed the car mass 900 kg to 1,000 kg so Delta p = 1000 x 20 = 20,000 kg m/s. Misconception expect recomputed.

Every misconception was missing the required expect key (validator fail) and merely restated the method. Rewrote each as honest diagnosis with a determinate wrong-answer expect derived by committing the error (add-instead-of-multiply, multiply-instead-of-divide, use-shorter-time, report-momentum-not-speed, assume-equal-speeds).

notes: g not used in this lesson (Newton's laws / momentum / waves), so no g=9.8 dependency. All given quantities were already in base units (kg, m/s, m, s, Hz), so no unit-conversion box was needed in any walk; walks kept lean. LADDER: bronze is mostly single-equation (B4 a=F/m and B3 lambda=v/f are mild single-step rearranges, acceptable for a drill lesson); silver adds rearrange + one standard-form problem; gold is genuinely multi-step (impulse-then-speed, conservation of momentum).
